title: A scorching soufflé
caption: Wind and thick cloud at sunset over the Chajnantor plateau, ALMA Observatory, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Heavy cloud rolls in over the high plateau of Chajnantor as the Sun goes down, pushed along by strong winds and lit in fiery colours. The plateau sits 5000 metres above sea level in the Chilean Andes and hosts the 66 antennas of the ALMA Observatory, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array.

Cloud is a rare visitor over these skies. ESO Photo Ambassador Babak Tafreshi took the picture while on the ESO 2016 Fulldome Expedition, a trip that gathered images for the ESO Supernova Planetarium & Visitor Centre.

The clouds ALMA is built to study are of a very different kind. Molecular clouds are huge gatherings of gas and dust, so cold that they sit just a few tens of degrees above absolute zero. Many of these star-forming regions look dark and hidden in visible light, yet they glow brightly at millimetre and submillimetre wavelengths, the light ALMA collects.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph of the ALMA site by Babak Tafreshi. The source gives no camera or colour details.
understand.eye: The antennas themselves work at millimetre and submillimetre wavelengths, which the eye cannot see, while this photograph records ordinary visible light.
